M5 Slice 3 — the shape I'm building
New — DataAccess (1 file)
src/MyRestaurant.DataAccess/Sittings/SittingRecordReads.cs — ISittingRecordReads/DapperSittingRecordReads, returning the complete stored record §11.4 demands: every order in a sitting, every event on it with the actor's resolved name and the stored event_type/actor_role as strings (the MenuItemEventEntry precedent — an enum is a projection with a failure mode), and every operation with the line's menu-item name joined back through order_operation_line_added.order_line_identifier, which the schema makes NOT NULL UNIQUE so that join is exact. Three queries regardless of order count.

Edited — WebApplication (3 files)

Sittings/SittingWorkflow.cs — ISittingWorkflow grows CloseManyAsync, looping §5.3's transaction once per sitting so each close is separately counted and separately broadcast. Returns an EndOfDayResult carrying every CloseSittingResult plus the counts.
Tables/TablesServiceCollectionExtensions.cs — one registration.
Components/Pages/Administration/AdministrationHome.razor + AdministrationMenu.razor + AdministrationTables.razor — a Sittings link in the header actions.
New — surfaces (2 files, static SSR)

/administration/sittings — open sittings with §5.4's last-activity timestamps, a checkbox per row, "Close selected". No select-all, nothing pre-ticked — closing twelve tables costs twelve deliberate ticks, and that is the confirmation rather than a second page. Recently-settled list below.
/administration/sittings/{SittingId:guid} — the record: header with both totals, roster, per-order full event stream, and §6.7's corrective forms only when the sitting is closed. While it's open the page links to /counter/sittings/{id} — an administrator passes area.counter, and §6.7 is named "post-close" for a reason. Corrections use the single-picker-at-the-bottom shape TableDisplays.razor and CounterSitting.razor already established, since per-row forms in static SSR need collection binding I can't compile-check.
Tests (2 files) — Testcontainers facts for the record reads, and a container-free wiring/behaviour file for the batch close over a hand-written ISittingSettlement fake (F-20).

Files to delete: none. No migration, no new packages, Program.cs untouched.

One flag before I write it: the batch-close form is the first place in this repo that reads raw POST values (await HttpContext.Request.ReadFormAsync()) rather than binding a [SupplyParameterFromForm] model, because §5.4 says "select" and a dynamic checkbox set has no static model. If you'd rather I avoid the new pattern, say so and I'll do per-row single-sitting Close buttons plus a "close every open sitting" action instead — cheaper, but it isn't quite what §5.4 describes.

Files to delete: none
Nothing renamed, nothing superseded, no migration, no packages, Program.cs untouched. git status will show exactly 12 files, all modified or added.

New (6): SittingRecordReads.cs, AdministrationSittings.razor, ManageSitting.razor, two test files, the docs append.
Edited (5): SittingWorkflow.cs (CloseAndSettleAsync untouched — verified by diff), TablesServiceCollectionExtensions.cs (one registration), and one <a> each in AdministrationHome/Menu/Tables.

Three decisions you may want to overrule
The batch-close form reads its own POST values. await HttpContext.Request.ReadFormAsync(...) — the first place in the tree that does. A checkbox set whose length is however many tables are open has no static model to bind, and the select-one picker used on ManageTable/TableDisplays isn't what §5.4's "select, close each" describes. It's not a second body read: Blazor already parsed the form to find the handler and HttpRequest caches it.

No select-all, nothing pre-ticked. Twelve tables cost twelve deliberate ticks, and that is the confirmation step. A select-all beside an irreversible action at the end of a long shift felt like the wrong thing to build; say the word and I'll add one.

Corrections only render once the sitting is settled. §6.7 is titled "post-close", and an administrator already passes area.counter, so an open table links to /counter/sittings/{id} rather than duplicating those controls. The record renders either way.

Where to look if it breaks
Two InputNumber bindings in ManageSitting.razor — decimal for the price (proven by ManageMenuItem) and int for quantity (new). If inference misbehaves, write TValue out explicitly; the exact fix is in _CHANGES.md.

Also, unrelated housekeeping: docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md is missing the appends for M4 slices 2–4 and M5 slice 1 — the headings jump from "M4 Slice 1" to "M5 Slice 2". Four cat commands (listed in _CHANGES.md) close the gap; nothing depends on it.

M5 after this is hide/unhide (§6.8) plus the hidden-records view, and the cross-cutting event explorer. ISittingRecordReads is the order half of that explorer's engine, IMenuEventLog the menu half, ISecurityEventLog the third — what's missing is order_visibility_event's write path and one screen over all three.
